title: roadmap
content:
Absolutely. Since you already know SQL, I’ll use SQL as the comparison point wherever it helps, but I won’t assume you know MongoDB concepts.

We’ll learn MongoDB from zero → project-ready, not just syntax. The goal is that by the end you can confidently use MongoDB in a real backend project with Python/FastAPI/Flask.

🗺️ MongoDB — Complete Roadmap

PHASE 0 — Setup & Mental Model

  • What is MongoDB?

  • SQL vs NoSQL

  • MongoDB vs MySQL/PostgreSQL

  • Document database concept

  • Database → Collection → Document → Field

  • BSON vs JSON

  • MongoDB architecture

  • MongoDB Atlas vs Local MongoDB

  • Install MongoDB / MongoDB Compass

  • Install MongoDB Shell (mongosh)

  • Create MongoDB Atlas account

  • Connect to MongoDB

  • Understand connection strings

  • First database + collection + document

PHASE 1 — MongoDB CRUD Fundamentals

1. Databases & Collections

  • Create database

  • Create collection

  • List databases

  • List collections

  • Delete collection

  • Delete database

2. Documents

  • JSON-like documents

  • Fields

  • Nested documents

  • Arrays

  • _id

  • ObjectId

3. INSERT

  • insertOne()

  • insertMany()

  • Automatically generated _id

  • Custom _id

  • Nested documents

  • Arrays

4. READ

  • find()

  • findOne()

  • Query filters

  • Comparison operators

    • $eq

    • $ne

    • $gt

    • $gte

    • $lt

    • $lte

    • $in

    • $nin

  • Logical operators

    • $and

    • $or

    • $not

    • $nor

5. UPDATE

  • updateOne()

  • updateMany()

  • replaceOne()

  • $set

  • $unset

  • $inc

  • $mul

  • $min

  • $max

  • $rename

  • Updating arrays

6. DELETE

  • deleteOne()

  • deleteMany()

PHASE 2 — Querying Like a Pro

This is where MongoDB starts becoming powerful.

Filtering

  • Multiple conditions

  • Nested fields

  • Array queries

  • Object queries

  • Regex

  • Existence checks

  • Data type checks

Projection

  • Selecting specific fields

  • Excluding fields

  • _id behavior

Sorting

  • sort()

  • Ascending

  • Descending

Pagination

  • limit()

  • skip()

  • Offset pagination

  • Cursor-based pagination

Counting

  • countDocuments()

  • estimatedDocumentCount()

PHASE 3 — Arrays & Nested Documents

Very important because MongoDB's document model differs heavily from SQL.

Arrays

  • Array fields

  • Querying arrays

  • $elemMatch

  • $all

  • $size

  • Adding elements

  • Removing elements

  • Updating array elements

  • Positional operator $

  • $[]

  • $[identifier]

Nested Documents

  • Embedded documents

  • Dot notation

  • Updating nested fields

  • Querying nested objects

PHASE 4 — Data Modeling

🔥 One of the most important phases

In SQL, you're usually taught:

Normalize → tables → relationships → JOIN

MongoDB requires a different way of thinking.

Relationships

  • One-to-one

  • One-to-many

  • Many-to-many

Embedding vs Referencing

  • When to embed

  • When to reference

  • Pros/cons

  • Avoiding excessive nesting

  • Avoiding giant documents

SQL → MongoDB Conversion

We'll take SQL schemas and convert them into MongoDB designs.

Example:

text
SQL

users
orders
order_items
products

vs.

text
MongoDB

users
orders
products

and decide what should actually be embedded/referenced.

PHASE 5 — Indexing & Performance

This is where you'll move from "I know MongoDB" to "I can use MongoDB in production."

Index Fundamentals

  • What is an index?

  • Why indexes matter

  • Collection scan

  • Index scan

Creating Indexes

  • createIndex()

  • Single-field indexes

  • Compound indexes

  • Unique indexes

  • Multikey indexes

  • Text indexes

Index Management

  • getIndexes()

  • dropIndex()

  • Index tradeoffs

Query Performance

  • explain()

  • Query plans

  • Winning plan

  • COLLSCAN

  • IXSCAN

PHASE 6 — Aggregation Framework

🔥 Extremely important for projects and interviews

Think of this as MongoDB's answer to complex SQL data processing.

We'll learn:

  • Aggregation concept

  • Aggregation pipeline

  • $match

  • $project

  • $group

  • $sort

  • $limit

  • $skip

  • $count

  • $unwind

  • $lookup

  • $addFields

  • $set

  • $replaceRoot

  • $facet

  • $bucket

And most importantly:

SQL → Aggregation Translation

sql
SELECT department, AVG(salary)
FROM employees
GROUP BY department;

→ MongoDB aggregation pipeline.

We'll practice this heavily.

PHASE 7 — MongoDB Relationships & Joins

Yes, MongoDB can do joins.

  • $lookup

  • $lookup with pipeline

  • $unwind

  • One-to-one joins

  • One-to-many joins

  • Many-to-many patterns

  • When $lookup is appropriate

  • When you should redesign the schema instead

PHASE 8 — Transactions & Data Consistency

Coming from SQL, this will be important.

  • What is a transaction?

  • MongoDB transactions

  • Sessions

  • Multi-document transactions

  • ACID

  • Commit

  • Abort

  • Error handling

  • When transactions are actually needed

PHASE 9 — MongoDB with Python

Now we'll connect MongoDB to actual application code.

PyMongo

  • Install PyMongo

  • Connection

  • MongoClient

  • Database objects

  • Collection objects

  • CRUD from Python

  • ObjectId in Python

  • Error handling

  • Environment variables

  • Connection pooling

Example architecture:

text
Python Application
       ↓
    PyMongo
       ↓
    MongoDB

PHASE 10 — MongoDB + FastAPI

🔥 This is where we'll make it project-ready.

  • MongoDB connection

  • FastAPI routes

  • CRUD API

  • Request validation

  • Response models

  • ObjectId handling

  • Error handling

  • Dependency management

  • Environment variables

  • Async MongoDB concepts

  • Database layer / repository pattern

Architecture:

text
Client
   ↓
FastAPI
   ↓
Routes
   ↓
Service Layer
   ↓
Database Layer
   ↓
MongoDB

PHASE 11 — ODMs

We'll understand what an ODM is and whether/when to use one.

Pydantic + MongoDB

  • Schema validation

  • Serialization

  • Deserialization

  • ObjectId handling

ODM Concepts

  • What is an ODM?

  • Document models

  • Relationships

  • Validation

  • Beanie / modern MongoDB tooling

  • ODM vs raw PyMongo

We'll learn raw MongoDB/PyMongo first, so you actually understand what's happening underneath.

PHASE 12 — Schema Validation

MongoDB is flexible, but flexible ≠ no structure.

  • Why schema validation matters

  • JSON Schema

  • Required fields

  • Data types

  • Validation rules

  • Validation levels

  • Validation actions

PHASE 13 — Security

Project-level security.

  • Authentication

  • Authorization

  • Database users

  • Roles

  • Permissions

  • Connection string security

  • Environment variables

  • IP/network access

  • MongoDB Atlas security basics

  • Never exposing credentials

PHASE 14 — MongoDB Atlas

We'll learn how to actually use MongoDB in a deployed project.

  • Create cluster

  • Database user

  • Network access

  • Connection URI

  • Connect application

  • Environment variables

  • Monitoring

  • Backups basics

  • Atlas UI

  • Compass

PHASE 15 — Production Concepts

Things you need to know before saying:

"I can use MongoDB in projects."

  • Connection pooling

  • Read/write concerns

  • Replication

  • Replica sets

  • High availability

  • Write concern

  • Read concern

  • Read preference

  • Sharding

  • Horizontal scaling

  • CAP theorem context

  • Eventual consistency

  • Backup & restore

  • Monitoring

We won't go absurdly deep into DBA territory, but you'll understand what these things mean and when they matter.

PHASE 16 — Real-World Project 🛠️

We'll build an actual backend rather than doing only isolated examples.

Project: E-Commerce / Inventory API

We'll implement:

text
Users
Products
Categories
Cart
Orders
Reviews
Payments

Features:

  • User CRUD

  • Product CRUD

  • Search

  • Filtering

  • Pagination

  • Sorting

  • Categories

  • Product reviews

  • Cart

  • Orders

  • Aggregation

  • $lookup

  • Indexes

  • Transactions

  • Authentication

  • FastAPI

  • MongoDB Atlas

  • Environment variables

  • Proper project structure

PHASE 17 — Advanced / Interview Level

After you're comfortable building projects:

  • Aggregation optimization

  • Advanced indexing

  • Partial indexes

  • Sparse indexes

  • TTL indexes

  • Geospatial queries

  • Text search

  • Change streams

  • Transactions deep dive

  • Replica sets

  • Sharding

  • Performance optimization

  • Common MongoDB interview questions

  • SQL → MongoDB problem conversion

🧠 How I'll Teach You

We'll not do this like:

"Here's find(). Memorize it."

Instead, every topic will follow this pattern:

1️⃣ Concept

I'll explain what it is and why it exists.

2️⃣ SQL Comparison

Since you know SQL:

text
SQL                  MongoDB
────────────────────────────────
Database             Database
Table                Collection
Row                  Document
Column               Field
JOIN                 $lookup
WHERE                Query filter
GROUP BY             $group
ORDER BY             $sort

This will make the transition much easier.

3️⃣ Visual Mental Model

For example:

text
MongoDB
│
├── Database
│      │
│      ├── Collection
│      │      ├── Document
│      │      ├── Document
│      │      └── Document
│      │
│      └── Collection
│
└── Collection

4️⃣ We'll Actually Type Commands

I'll make you run commands rather than just reading them.

5️⃣ Exercises

I'll give you tasks like:

Create a students collection and insert 5 students.

You'll do it.

Then we'll check it.

6️⃣ Real Project Thinking

I'll constantly explain:

"In an actual backend, why would we do this?"

🏁 Final Skill Level

By the end, you should be able to look at something like:

text
User
 ├── orders
 ├── addresses
 └── preferences

Product
 ├── category
 ├── reviews
 └── inventory

and independently decide:

"Should this be embedded, referenced, indexed, aggregated, or handled through a transaction?"

That's the actual goal—not memorizing 50 MongoDB commands.

🚀 Our Starting Point

We'll start with:

PART 1 — MongoDB Setup + First Database

We'll cover:

text
1. What MongoDB actually is
2. SQL vs MongoDB mental model
3. MongoDB architecture
4. MongoDB Atlas
5. Local MongoDB
6. MongoDB Compass
7. mongosh
8. Installation/setup
9. Connecting to MongoDB
10. Creating our first database
11. Creating our first collection
12. Inserting our first document
13. Reading it back
14. Understanding _id and ObjectId

And we'll do it hands-on, with you actually creating the database and running the commands on your machine.

No prior MongoDB knowledge assumed.
